query: For AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock intended for additively manufactured miniature components, what single intervention could overcome the residual thermal stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and processing complexity associated with mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions, states the applicable processing window, geometry, and test conditions, identifies supporting prior evidence, and describes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Solid‐state friction stir deposition (FSD) of AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock produces miniature additively manufactured components with substantially lower residual thermal stresses, finer equiaxed microstructures, and improved mechanical properties compared to conventional laser powder bed fusion (LPBF).
generation.material_initial_state: Vacuum‐atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder (15–45 μm), as‐atomized feedstock with homogeneous composition.
generation.intervention: Friction stir deposition using a rotating tool (1500 rpm) traversing at 100 mm/min, depositing 0.5 mm layers on an Al substrate preheated to 50 °C in argon.
generation.conditions: Tool rotation 1000–2000 rpm, traverse speed 50–150 mm/min, layer thickness 0.3–1.0 mm, inert gas atmosphere, component feature size ≤20 mm, ambient‐temperature testing.
generation.structural_mediator: Ultrafine equiaxed grains (~1 μm) formed by dynamic recrystallization; elimination of columnar solidification structures.
generation.mechanism: Severe plastic deformation in the solid state drives dynamic recrystallization and avoids melting/rapid solidification, thus reducing thermal gradients and locking in low residual stress while refining grains.
generation.predicted_outcome: Residual stress <30 MPa (vs ~200 MPa LPBF); ultimate tensile strength ~480 MPa (vs ~400 MPa LPBF); elongation-to-failure ~6.5% (vs ~5% LPBF).
generation.baseline: Components made by LPBF at 200 W, 1200 mm/s, 30 μm layer, no preheat: residual stress ~200 MPa, UTS ~400 MPa, elongation ~5%.
generation.boundary: Valid for AlCrFeNiSi powder 15–45 μm, component thickness ≤5 mm, FSD parameters as specified, inert gas processing, ambient mechanical testing.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—FSD is established for Al alloys but direct data on AlCrFeNiSi high‐entropy alloy are limited; magnitude of improvements may vary.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate miniature tensile coupons via FSD (specified parameters) and via baseline LPBF. Characterize residual stress by XRD, grain size by EBSD, tensile properties per ASTM E8 subsize, and microhardness maps.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if FSD parts do not achieve ≥50% reduction in residual stress (i.e. remain >100 MPa) OR do not show ≥10% increase in UTS OR show no improvement in elongation relative to LPBF baseline.
